hypotheses.claim: Allowing online adaptation during perturbation attenuates delayed lesion loss relative to acute frozen-learning lesion loss for redundant/plastic FRANK pathways.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Compensation is negligible at relevant FRANK timescales, so acute and delayed lesion rankings match.
hypotheses.prediction: For at least some H1 pathways, chronic lesion loss after a fixed learning budget is materially smaller than acute frozen-learning loss.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across preregistered H1 episodes/pathways, frozen-vs-allowed learning produces no material change in lesion effect or causal ranking.

hypotheses.claim: A mechanism can be causally necessary in the pre-lesion state yet show near-zero chronic lesion effect after adaptation.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Recovered chronic function implies the lesioned mechanism was not necessary in the original state.
hypotheses.prediction: Common-snapshot acute lesion shows large loss while the same lesion after adaptation shows near-baseline performance plus measurable rerouting/parameter change.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any pathway with near-zero chronic lesion effect also has near-zero acute frozen-learning effect from the same pre-lesion snapshot.

hypotheses.claim: Mechanism-only rescue after adaptive compensation can under-recover or worsen outcome unless learner state is rolled back or counterfactually matched.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Restoring the lesioned mechanism is sufficient regardless of adaptation history.
hypotheses.prediction: Some adapted states show worse outcome after mechanism-only rescue than immediately before rescue, while full state rollback restores baseline.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across H1 adaptive lesions, mechanism-only rescue is statistically equivalent to state-rollback/counterfactual-twin rescue.

hypotheses.claim: Perturbation duty cycle is part of causal measurement identity because it changes adaptation opportunity and therefore measured chronic effect.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Only cumulative lesion exposure matters; schedule does not affect inferred causal role.
hypotheses.prediction: Continuous vs intermittent perturbation with declared matched budgets yields different compensation trajectories and chronic readouts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Duty cycle never changes compensation or causal ranking after matched exposure/data/compute controls.

hypotheses.claim: A two-window protocol separating acute frozen-learning necessity from chronic adaptive compensation is more informative than a single lesion metric.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A single delayed lesion/rescue metric is sufficient for causal interpretation.
hypotheses.prediction: The pair (acute_loss, compensation_gain) predicts cross-context/cross-implementation outcomes better than chronic_loss alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: Two-window metrics add no out-of-sample predictive or falsification value over the best single lesion metric.
